R2 REPORT: cognitive-skill routing (creativity / logic-science / design / business / marketing)

VERDICT (my belief): NOT a general upgrade. Each mechanism helps only when its world assumption holds. It costs 1-3 points otherwise. The held-out wins come from worlds A and C, which share the same specialist/multimodal structure, so I would not count them as more than one independent world.

FILES
- C:\Users\mariu\neural-mesh\src\cognition.rs (new; world, mechanisms, 9 unit tests). I appended one line, `pub mod cognition;`, to src/lib.rs.
- C:\Users\mariu\neural-mesh\src\bin\r2_cognition.rs (new)
- C:\Users\mariu\neural-mesh\results\r2_cognition.json (output)
- I appended my section to C:\Users\mariu\neural-mesh\results\research_board.md (one `cat >>`).

RERUN (about 1 minute)
```
export PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:/c/Users/mariu/AppData/Local/Microsoft/WinGet/Packages/BrechtSanders.WinLibs.POSIX.UCRT_Microsoft.Winget.Source_8wekyb3d8bbwe/mingw64/bin:$PATH"
export CARGO_TARGET_DIR=C:/Users/mariu/nm-target-r2
cargo run --release --bin r2_cognition -- --out results/r2_cognition.json
cargo test --release --lib cognition
```
Tests: all 9 cognition tests pass. The full `cargo test --release --lib` is not green. 3 `coupling::` tests fail, in another team's file, not mine.

PROTOCOL
- Every learner, baselines and mechanisms alike, is tuned per world on seeds 1-8 only.
- Evaluation is on held-out seeds 31-60, paired 95% t-CI, Holm over 160 tests across all worlds and hypotheses.
- Fair baselines are keyword, eps-greedy (tuned), pooled-thompson (tuned), hebbian-robust, and warm(hebbian-robust) (tuned). The same learner is used in all three stages (plan, build, critique).
- I always compare against the best baseline by held-out mean, which was warm(hebbian-robust) in every world.

WORLD (all assumptions are listed in the JSON)
- 5 domains. Coding, science and business are correctness; design and marketing are creative. The router is told which is which.
- Each task is plan, then build, then critique, with a separate router per stage.
- Creative value is quality x (0.4 + 0.6 x novelty). Novelty is measured against the last 10 solutions in the domain, shared across all agents.
- Agents have a habit approach used with probability 0.85, so flat agent routing cannot steer style.
- Critic gain is p(1-p)(sens-fa) minus a 0.02 cost. A critic with sens < fa hurts.
- Four world variants:
  - A: specialists plus multimodal creative, where several agents with distinct styles reach similar quality. This is the assumption that favours the creative mechanisms.
  - B: generalists, a single-peak creative domain, noise 0.15, and drift at task 700.
  - C: same as A but novelty is worth 0.
  - D: rigged-check. Generalists, equal critics, approach irrelevant to quality, and approach labels unrelated to the solution embeddings.
- The mechanisms read extra signals the baselines do not see: the observed approach label, a quality score separate from novelty, and the critic's verdict checked against later ground truth.

RESULTS (held-out, diff [95% CI], Holm-corrected)
- M1, quality-diversity niche archive plus creative-only novelty, vs the flat best learner on creative-domain value:
  - A: +0.032 [.025,.039], WIN.
  - B: -0.014, LOSE.
  - C: +0.033, but the same archive without novelty gets +0.037. The gain is niche steering, not novelty.
  - D: -0.028, LOSE.
  - Novelty bonus isolated (same archive, bonus on vs off): A +0.076 [.069,.082]; B, C and D within -0.004 to -0.003 (C is -0.004, p=.03). So a useless bonus costs almost nothing.
- M2, novelty bonus on agent arms (no style steering), creative-only vs the same learner without the bonus:
  - A: +0.041 [.035,.048], WIN.
  - B, C, D: ns (+0.007, +0.001, +0.002).
  - Control, novelty applied to ALL domains: correctness value drops by 0.038 to 0.047 in every world (Holm-significant). Creative-only never hurt correctness (|diff| < 0.003, ns).
- M3, generator then critic:
  - Any critic beats none by +0.03 to +0.07 in all worlds.
  - Learned critic (verdict-label signal) vs random and fixed: A +0.038 and +0.030, WIN. C +0.036 and +0.031, WIN. B +0.007 and +0.004, ns. D +0.001 and +0.001, ns, which is the rigged world behaving as designed.
  - Learned critic from final reward only is weak. In A it is +0.009 vs random, ns (Holm .26).
  - NEGATIVE: neither learned critic beats the fair warm(hebbian-robust) bandit used as critic selector. A -0.008 (verdict) and -0.037 (final reward). B -0.014, C -0.007, D +0.001 ns.
  - The tuned system composition therefore kept the fair critic in all four worlds.
- M4, hierarchical (per-domain learners) vs flat: A +0.023 [.020,.025] WIN, C +0.017 WIN, B -0.0125 (Holm p=.04) LOSE, D -0.004 ns. It helps only with specialists.
- S, system (hierarchical + QD niche build + fair critic) vs the best fair baseline, overall:

| World | Overall diff [95% CI] | Result |
|---|---|---|
| A | +0.032 [.028,.037] | WIN (first 300 tasks +0.019, WIN) |
| C | +0.028 [.024,.032] | WIN (first 300 tasks +0.030) |
| B | -0.012 [-.018,-.005] | LOSE (first 300 tasks -0.027) |
| D | -0.019 [-.024,-.014] | LOSE |

- Rigged-check D: no false positives among the mechanism-vs-fair tests.

CAVEATS
- The world is mine. Habit 0.85 and novelty weight 0.6 were set a priori, not swept.
- The QD learner has no keyword prior or topic features, so it carries a learner-quality handicap that shows up in B and D.
- The pyribs cross-check was NOT done. No Python venv exists and I installed no packages, so archive behaviour is covered only by unit tests.
- No security findings, since nothing was installed. No other agents' files were edited.
- I have not applied the board-level accept/reject decision.
